prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at magic twist angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, opening the field of moiré quantum matter.

statement.case_for: After the full round-1 exchange I keep B001 alone, with MacDonald, Bistritzer and Jarillo-Herrero, and my configuration has not changed since round 1. The deciding point for me is what the 'discovery or invention' criterion asks us to fix in a citation. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model made a specific, falsifiable statement (flat bands at a magic angle), and the 2018 experiments found correlated insulators and superconductivity in that regime. Independent groups have reproduced the phases and carried them into twisted multilayers, twisted TMDs and fractional Chern insulators. None of that depends on the pairing mechanism, so a citation limited to the prediction and the observed phases is not hostage to the open question. As an experimentalist I also value that the claim is tested by many different samples and laboratories, which answers the worry that the result rests on delicate devices. The chair asks which criterion decides between B001 and B007. For me it is a discovery in nature that was predicted quantitatively and then opened a new class of tunable matter, weighed against a clean invention whose largest payoff, the redefinition of the second, is still prospective. Both are mature and I would defend either. I put B001 first on the science, and I do not rely on the opening support counts.
statement.case_against: The reservations are real. The pairing mechanism and several correlated states are still debated, twist-angle disorder and device variability complicate comparison across laboratories, and the field is moving fast enough that a later reading of the superconductivity could change how the story is told. The experimental credit is thin: Cao as first author, Fatemi, and the Dean, Efetov, Young and Yazdani groups fall outside the three names, and earlier twisted-graphene band-structure theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto; Suarez Morell and colleagues) has a claim on the theory side that the citation wording must respect. B007 is the stronger configuration on cleanliness of attribution (two names, no contest among the eight members) and on the stability of what is being claimed. If the committee decided that an unsettled interpretation outweighs field-opening novelty, B007 would be the better prize this year.

responses.point: Kroll holds B001 as an alternative because the superconducting mechanism is unsettled and the lattice clock is a finished capability with stable interpretation, and he asks whether B030 is an instrumentation prize or a physics discovery.
responses.response: I accept the clock is the cleaner attribution, and I do not think it is the weaker science. Where I differ is on what is unsettled. The mechanism is open but the phenomenon is not: the correlated insulators and superconducting domes have been reproduced by several groups, which is the evidence I would use to judge maturity as an experimentalist. The redefinition of the second is also still pending, so both candidates carry an open item and I do not read yours as decisive. On B030, since you asked, I see it as an instrument invention whose value shows up in materials physics, chemistry and nanoscience. That is a legitimate basis for the prize, but the Krivanek claim, the TEM and STEM split and the absence of any ranking from other members mean I will not press it. I also note your Hall and JILA disclosure and agree it should be recorded, with the committee hearing the B007 case from others as well.

responses.point: Mehlig moved from a two-name B001 to the three-name set, and notes that precursors in twisted-graphene theory bear on the wording.
responses.response: I welcome the move to three names. The 2011 paper is a joint result and the magic angle comes from that calculation, so dropping Bistritzer would make the prediction credit incomplete. Your reminder about precursors is the point I most want the citation to carry. Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto and the Suarez Morell group worked on twisted-layer band structure earlier, so the wording should name the prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles from the continuum model, and not twisted graphene or moiré physics in general. I would also keep your doubt about the mechanism in the citation, which should say nothing about explaining the superconductivity.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks the clock first because its claim is a measured number reproduced in several laboratories, while the twisted-graphene citation depends on a contested interpretation. She also separates the lattice from the 2005 comb.
responses.response: The distinction between the lattice and the comb is persuasive, and I accept that Katori's magic-wavelength idea is separable from the 2005 prize. I disagree with the premise that my B001 citation rests on interpretation. As drafted it credits a prediction and the observation of phases, both reproduced, and it is silent on the mechanism, so it has the same kind of measured-result footing as your clock claim. Your attribution argument is the stronger point against me, since the clock pair is uncontested while Cao and Fatemi stay outside my three names. I weigh that cost as real but smaller than the cost of passing over a prediction tested in nature. I would not object if the committee concluded otherwise, and B007 remains my first alternative.

responses.point: Danielsson argues that B001 opens a new class of tunable correlated matter, while the lattice clock refines an already honoured measurement line, and that B030 would be defensible only as an instrumentation prize.
responses.response: I agree with your account of why B001 leads, and I accept your reading that B030 is defensible but has an unresolved Krivanek problem. I would qualify the claim that B007 only refines an honoured line, because the lattice is a different method from the comb, as Lindroth argues. I would rest B001 on novelty of the physics, not on a weakness in the clock. I also want to repeat my round-1 point that independent confirming groups are evidence of maturity and not claimants who must be named, while the real attribution risk is on the theory side.

responses.point: Johansson would keep the three names and not trade a theorist for a wider experimental credit, and he states that the prize should reward a change in physical knowledge more than an improvement in how we see it.
responses.response: Thank you for the clear answer on Dean. I agree that the two decisive steps are the 2011 prediction and the 2018 discovery, and that widening the experimental credit would come at the cost of one of them. On your reservation about instrumentation, I accept that the corrector chiefly improved seeing, but atomic-resolution spectroscopy and imaging now shape physical knowledge about interfaces, defects and two-dimensional materials, which twisted bilayer work itself uses to check stacking and strain. That does not rescue B030 against its credit defect, and I still do not place it in the configuration. I would also note that you ranked B058 first and have said you would recuse on it, which seems the right handling.

uncertainties: Whether one experimental name, Jarillo-Herrero, fairly represents the 2018 discovery given Cao as first author and the Fatemi, Dean, Efetov, Young and Yazdani groups outside the limit.
How the citation should be worded to credit the continuum-model flat-band prediction without implying that earlier twisted-graphene band-structure work did not exist.
Whether the open pairing mechanism will, in the committee's judgement, still count as a maturity issue once the citation says nothing about the mechanism.
Whether B007 should be preferred in a year when attribution cleanliness is weighted over novelty, and how the committee treats the unfinished redefinition of the second.
Whether B030 could be reconsidered if the credited names were revisited to include Krivanek, which I cannot judge from the supplied names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with Allan H. MacDonald, Rafi Bistritzer or Pablo Jarillo-Herrero is documented in my profile. B030 (aberration-corrected electron optics) is in my own research field of electron microscopy. It is only an alternative, I documented no relationship with Rose, Urban or Haider, and I would recuse on any decision on B030 if the committee judged that necessary. My University of Tokyo fellowship and long-running exchanges with Japanese universities are a possible but undocumented link to B007 (Katori), which I disclose. I share Chalmers with Johansson, with no documented collaboration. I have noted Kroll's disclosed link to Hall's laboratory and JILA for B007, and Johansson's proximity to B058.
